Screen participants on their learning tests

Source: R/fba-screen-learning.R
screen_learning.Rd

Applies an exclusion criterion to the per-stage tests implemented in test_learning(). Which stages count to the exclusion decision and whether failing any or all of them excludes the participant is decided here, in stages and rule, respectively. The function Returns one row per participant with the decision and the reason for it, so that the excluded identifiers can be passed on to record_exclusion().

Usage

screen_learning(tests, stages = NULL, rule = c("any", "all"), silence = FALSE)

Arguments

tests

Per-participant, per-stage learning tests from test_learning().

stages

Character. Stages whose test counts towards the criterion. NULL (default) uses every stage in tests.

rule

Character(1). "any" (default) excludes a participant who fails the test in at least one of stages. "all" excludes only a participant who fails it in every one of stages.

silence

Logical(1). Suppress the message summarising the criterion and its yield. Defaults to FALSE (recommended).

Value

A tibble with one row per participant, and columns:

id

Participant identifier.

exclude

TRUE when the participant meets the exclusion criterion.

n_failed

Number of stages in which the participant did not score significantly above chance.

failed_stages

Failed stages, comma-separated; NA when none.

reason

For excluded participants, the failed tests in words, e.g. "Stage 3: 27/48 correct, below the cut-off of 29 (p = 0.235)"; NA for participants who are kept.

Details

A stage counts as failed when its test did find clear evidence of above-chance performance, including a stage without any answered trial.

The function makes exclusion decision, but it does not exclude. Exclusions are applied, and recorded in the provenance of the data bundle, by record_exclusion(), for instance with ids = screen$id[screen$exclude]. Its description should state the test, alpha, the stages and the rule, so that it can be reported verbatim.

Messages

Every call states the criterion, how many participants it excludes, and how many failed each of stages, unless silenced (silence = TRUE).

See also

test_learning(), record_exclusion()
